contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #193: Serre’s intersection-multiplicity conjecture.

Full hypotheses and categories of asymptotic.tex as:length-hypotheses through as:base-equality; ordinary negligible ranks, uniform bounded complexes, quotient support, and arbitrary idempotent summands.

definitions.A: excellent regular local Z_(p)-algebra of dimension e>0, maximal ideal J, regular parameters z_1,...,z_e
definitions.T: finite local A-domain with the same residue field; r=rank_A(T)
definitions.C: T-algebra with nonnegative additive length lambda on J-power torsion modules, zero positive parameter-Koszul lengths and lambda(C/(z_1^v,...,z_e^v)C)=v^e r for every v>=1
definitions.P_S: idempotent completion of D_S/N_S; D_S is the uniform bounded perfect hull of free sequences of ranks O(s_n); N_S is thickly generated by ordinary o(s_n) rank sequences
definitions.supported: for some fixed v every z_j^v annihilates the identity in the category containing the object
definitions.length_quotient: Serre quotient by zero normalized ultralimit length, not by ordinary negligible rank

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 193 (Serre’s intersection-multiplicity conjecture.; papers: Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
thm:main: strict positivity of Serre intersection multiplicity for nonzero finite modules of complementary dimensions and finite-length tensor product over a Noetherian regular local ring.
pos:reduction and pos:vanishing: reduce to complete prime quotients over an algebraically closed characteristic-p residue field, with positive complementary dimensions.
len:normalization and len:input: construct the finite regular bases, algebras and lengths with all asserted parameter properties.
ds:descent: invariant supported rational K-theory classes descend under the manuscript's finite-surjection and orbit hypotheses.
ds:ordinary-norm: ordinary and normalized evaluations agree on the ordinary Galois norm sums.
pos:first-average: the first Galois norm expresses a positive scalar multiple of the intersection multiplicity as the sum of c_sigma.
as:supported-quotient: supported roofs compute the full supported subquotient, and every supported quotient object is a retract of a uniformly supported bounded free lift.
as:evaluations and its A version: homology lengths descend to supported quotients, extend to idempotent images, are finite and nonnegative, and have additive Euler sums.
as:finite-tor and ds:finite-length-basechange: the stated parameter-length hypotheses imply zero positive Tor length and multiplication of finite-length zero Tor by r.
Both finite comparison spectral sequences, together with their finite filtered abutments and natural scalar-extension identifications, invert supported-small-cone maps in the length quotients.

Compatible idempotent images preserve exact sequences and homology; on an invariant filtration the image intersects each step in its projected step, and the associated graded image is the image of the graded projector.
Finite spectral-page Euler cancellation and finite-filtration additivity apply to the localized idempotent images; the first-page ordinary weight is the alternating rank of a resolution of T.

as:base-equality under its full hypotheses: chi_ord(X tensor_A^L T) = rank_A(T) chi_A(X) = chi_C(X tensor_A^L T) for every supported X in P_A, including quotient-only support and nonlifting idempotents.
as:connective and the support identification supply a connective coefficient algebra compatible with scalar extension and central localization.
as:norm: the ordinary and normalized evaluations agree on supported Galois norm sums in the asymptotic category.
pos:parameters, pos:tor-bound and pos:approximation: obtain the parameter quotient, finite Tor range, action-preserving finite-length approximations and positive generator density.
pos:supported-truncation: truncated minimal resolutions yield supported quotient objects with the required ordinary evaluation.
pos:positive-evaluation: the normalized asymptotic evaluation is strictly positive.
pos:second-average: the second Galois average makes every c_sigma strictly positive.

claims.natural_statement: For modules over any ring, commuting idempotents preserve exactness at the middle and surjectivity of an exact sequence after restriction to their ranges; for an invariant submodule F and an idempotent p, range(p) intersect F equals p(F). This module core does not assert construction of the manuscript quotient or its spectral sequences.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Map

namespace SupportedEuler

variable {R M N Q : Type*} [Ring R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
variable [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]

theorem fixed_of_mem_range
    (p : M →ₗ[R] M) (hp : p.comp p = p)
    {x : M} (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range p) : p x = x := by
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hx
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun hp y

theorem range_inter_eq_map
    (p : M →ₗ[R] M) (hp : p.comp p = p)
    (F : Submodule R M) (hF : ∀ x ∈ F, p x ∈ F) :
    LinearMap.range p ⊓ F = F.map p := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro x hx
    exact ⟨x, hx.2, fixed_of_mem_range p hp hx.1⟩
  · intro x hx
    obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := hx
    exact ⟨⟨y, rfl⟩, hF y hy⟩

theorem exact_on_ranges
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] Q)
    (a : M →ₗ[R] M) (b : N →ₗ[R] N)
    (hb : b.comp b = b) (hfa : f.comp a = b.comp f)
    (hex : ∀ y : N, g y = 0 ↔ ∃ x : M, f x = y) :
    ∀ y : N, y ∈ LinearMap.range b →
      (g y = 0 ↔ ∃ x : M, x ∈ LinearMap.range a ∧ f x = y) := by
  intro y hy
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (hex y).mp h
    refine ⟨a x, ⟨x, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    calc
      f (a x) = b (f x) := DFunLike.congr_fun hfa x
      _ = b y := congrArg b hx
      _ = y := fixed_of_mem_range b hb hy
  · rintro ⟨x, _, hx⟩
    exact (hex y).mpr ⟨x, hx⟩

theorem surjective_on_ranges
    (g : N →ₗ[R] Q) (b : N →ₗ[R] N) (c : Q →ₗ[R] Q)
    (hc : c.comp c = c) (hgc : g.comp b = c.comp g)
    (hgs : Function.Surjective g) :
    ∀ z : Q, z ∈ LinearMap.range c →
      ∃ y : N, y ∈ LinearMap.range b ∧ g y = z := by
  intro z hz
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hgs z
  refine ⟨b y, ⟨y, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  calc
    g (b y) = c (g y) := DFunLike.congr_fun hgc y
    _ = c z := congrArg c hy
    _ = z := fixed_of_mem_range c hc hz

theorem injective_on_range
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (a : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Function.Injective (fun x : LinearMap.range a => f x) := by
  intro x y h
  exact Subtype.ext (hf h)

theorem invariant_quotient_fixed_lift
    (p : M →ₗ[R] M) (hp : p.comp p = p)
    (F G : Submodule R M) (hG : ∀ x ∈ G, p x ∈ G)
    {x : M} (hxG : x ∈ G) (hxF : p x - x ∈ F) :
    ∃ y : M, y ∈ G ∧ p y = y ∧ y - x ∈ F := by
  refine ⟨p x, hG x hxG, ?_, hxF⟩
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun hp x

end SupportedEuler

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Projection

namespace SupportedEuler

variable {R M N Q : Type*} [Ring R]

variable [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
variable [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]

theorem fixed_of_mem_range
    (p : M →ₗ[R] M) (hp : p.comp p = p)
    {x : M} (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range p) : p x = x := by
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hx
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun hp y

    (p : M →ₗ[R] M) (hp : p.comp p = p)

  apply le_antisymm
  · intro x hx

    exact ⟨⟨y, rfl⟩, hF y hy⟩

theorem exact_on_ranges
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] Q)
    (a : M →ₗ[R] M) (b : N →ₗ[R] N)
    (hb : b.comp b = b) (hfa : f.comp a = b.comp f)
    (hex : ∀ y : N, g y = 0 ↔ ∃ x : M, f x = y) :
    ∀ y : N, y ∈ LinearMap.range b →
      (g y = 0 ↔ ∃ x : M, x ∈ LinearMap.range a ∧ f x = y) := by
  intro y hy
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (hex y).mp h
    refine ⟨a x, ⟨x, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    calc
      f (a x) = b (f x) := DFunLike.congr_fun hfa x

    (g : N →ₗ[R] Q) (b : N →ₗ[R] N) (c : Q →ₗ[R] Q)
    (hc : c.comp c = c) (hgc : g.comp b = c.comp g)
    (hgs : Function.Surjective g) :
    ∀ z : Q, z ∈ LinearMap.range c →
      ∃ y : N, y ∈ LinearMap.range b ∧ g y = z := by
  intro z hz
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hgs z
  refine ⟨b y, ⟨y, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  calc
    g (b y) = c (g y) := DFunLike.congr_fun hgc y
    _ = c z := congrArg c hy
    _ = z := fixed_of_mem_range c hc hz

    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (a : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Function.Injective (fun x : LinearMap.range a => f x) := by
  intro x y h
  exact Subtype.ext (hf h)

theorem invariant_quotient_fixed_lift
    (p : M →ₗ[R] M) (hp : p.comp p = p)

claims.natural_statement: For every supported quotient object X, H_i^C(X tensor_A^L T) is naturally isomorphic to the exact length-scaling tensor functor applied to H_i^A(X), including arbitrary quotient idempotent summands.

For A=F_p[[a,b]], T=A direct_sum (a,b)u inside C=F_p[[u,b]], a=u^2, all stated length hypotheses hold with rank two, while Tor(A/(a^m,b^q),T) has lengths 2mq+1 and 1 in degrees zero and one and Euler sum 2mq. The positive ordinary Tor term need not be negligible.

routes.retired_because: Raw homology of arbitrary unsupported lifts does not descend, as the manuscript already acknowledges in as:nonuniform-warning. That example kills this strategy, not as:base-equality.

The admissible domain T=A direct_sum (a,b)u over A=F_p[[a,b]] has length Tor_1(A/(a^m,b^q),T)=1; n copies normalized by s_n=n retain length one. Thus ordinary positive Tor cannot be discarded. This refutes the stronger strategy, not the manuscript Euler assertion.
